answer: Each new key must produce a memory-hard proof, filling 2 GB of scratch space and answering random reads against a Merkle root, bound to the registry's echo of the latest epoch seed. Walnut-sized RAM is the bottleneck: one machine can hold only so many tables, so 50 fake heads need 50 slots of memory, and the tide of renewals every epoch repeats the bill, making each extra identity add fresh hardware rent.
